keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Diepholz row). The page: 'at its greatest extent in the sixteenth century' it 'stretched from Colnrade and Goldenstedt in the north to Wehdem, Dielingen and Lemforde in the south' and 'the distance from the northernmost point to the southernmost point of the county was about 47 kilometers whilst the distance from east to west was 22 kilometers at its widest point'. Two 12 km circles at 8.37E 52.74N and 8.37E 52.50N (about 870 km2) are a soft stand-in; the infobox gives no area, and the page dates no earlier extent.

ledger.note: About 1070 or 1085 (infobox 'ca. 1070/1085-1585'; the page is silent on a founding date, and the lead dates the dynasty's rule to 'the late tenth century'). The family name 'first appears in 1160 (in Latinised German) as de Thefholte' and 'a continuous genealogy of the dynasty only starts with Gottschalk I (cited 1177-1205)'.

1285: the Blankena patrimony. 'in 1285, Konrad V, inherited the rich patrimony of the Lords of Blankena from his cousin, Hermann von Blankena' (page silent on where the lands lay; the circle is the core).

1291: Sudholte. The page speaks of 'the acquisition in 1291 of the Vicecomitat of Sudholte, which gave them full jurisdiction over their subjects in the parishes of Drebber, Barnstorf and Goldenstedt' (a fief of the Bishop of Munster for Barnstorf, Goldenstedt and Colnrade). The page names no seller; the circle is a stand-in for the three parishes.

region.text: the Vicecomitat of Sudholte (Drebber, Barnstorf, Goldenstedt)

ledger.note: 1510: Rudolf VIII 'abdicated his absolute sovereignty over Diepholz in 1510 and recognised the Duke of Brunswick-Luneburg as his liege lord' in return for protection; 'This agreement was only formally recognised as valid by the Emperor Maximilian I in 1517.' The tie ran to 1585.

region.text: the County of Diepholz under Brunswick-Luneburg's overlordship

ledger.note: 1521: Auburg. Friedrich I 'relinquished sovereignty over the territories around Auburg to Landgrave Philip I of Hesse in 1521, who subsequently re-enfeoffed him with them'. The page does not say where Auburg lay; the 6 km circle is a stand-in inside the county.

region.text: the territories around Auburg, held of Hesse

ledger.note: 1585: the Brunswick overlordship ends with the county. 'most of the county was therefore absorbed into the Welf duchy.'
1585: the Hessian tie on Auburg ends. 'Auburg and its surrounding territories fell to the Landgraviate of Hesse.'
1585: Auburg to Hesse. 'Auburg and its surrounding territories fell to the Landgraviate of Hesse.'

1585: the last count dies. 'Their son, Friedrich II, died in 1585, but only left a daughter, Anna Margaretha, who was unable to succeed according to the strictures of Saxon inheritance law'; 'most of the county was therefore absorbed into the Welf duchy' (infobox 'County of Diepholz absorbed by Duchy of Brunswick-Luneburg'). The Brunswick-Luneburg dossier carries the same transfer at 1584 (from the Calenberg page).

certainty.note: The page gives the sixteenth-century extent as two distances only; the circles are stand-ins, and Auburg's place is not on the page.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Diepholz row; the Brunswick-Luneburg dossier named it as a counterpart.

SCOPE. Infobox 'ca. 1070/1085-1585'; the start year 1070 is the infobox's first figure and is confidence 1 (the page is silent on a founding act). The page gives no capital (the field is blank), so none is entered.

SHAPES. Two 12 km circles at 8.37E 52.74N and 8.37E 52.50N (about 870 km2) for the sixteenth-century extent (47 km by 22 km); Sudholte circle 8.45E 52.69N 12 km; Auburg stand-in 8.55E 52.55N 6 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Diepholz', 'Barnstorf', 'Goldenstedt', 'Drebber', 'Lemforde', 'Colnrade', 'Auburg'.

CONFLICT WITH THE BRUNSWICK DOSSIER. This page ends the county in 1585 (lead 'until 1585'; Friedrich II 'died in 1585'); the Calenberg page cited in duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg says 'acquired Diepholz in 1584'. The two years are left as each page gives them. The page also says the sovereignty ceded in 1521 was 'that had not already been abdicated to the Dukes of Brunswick-Calenberg', which sits oddly with the 1510 abdication to Brunswick-Luneburg.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The founding year; (2) where Auburg lay; (3) the extent before the sixteenth century; (4) the Bronkhorst claim of 1553 is a claim only; (5) the 1441 dowry (Wagenfeld, Bokel, Struten) has no counterpart on the page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
